title: thread-scaling separates each tool's serial and parallel time
body:
thread-scaling's real set is all of Pfam against 500,000 MGnify sequences, sized so that serial work does not dominate any point, and it ran once with no `--reps`. On that run one slow single-thread mmseqs search skewed every efficiency point of its arm, since `parse` reads the percentage of perfect speedup against the lowest rung.

## Proposal
Measure each tool's serial and parallel time from outside the tool, with hmph, so that the set can shrink and `--reps` becomes affordable. A scaling point must not be dominated by fixed costs or by one noisy run.
close_reason: Dropped. thread-scaling measures no serial/parallel split. The 22 Oct node 1 run at three reps (5ee1285, f2bffd3) is the published measurement.

notes.author: jackroddy/01dd6c44
notes.text: The serial/parallel split is being built as its own tool, hmph, at ~/hmph (its own repo, its own foam). It watches a process tree and writes concurrency per process per tick, integrated into serial seconds and parallel work. Once it runs, wrap thread-scaling's searches in it rather than instrumenting the tools.

notes.author: jackroddy/0d39a02d
notes.text: hmph is dropped. Three reps replace it: the rerun uses nail dev 326797b (sha `8443291daa9f`) at `--rungs 1,2,4,8,16,32,48 --reps 3`, started 18 Oct 2026. nail now runs with `-s` and writes its stage tree to a `.stats` file beside each hit table, which gives nail's serial stages at every rung. mmseqs and hmmer get no serial split. The 26 September results are in `/data/thread-scaling-bk-2026-09-26`.
